name: pain
description: The feeling of a physical or mental injury. Ranges from intense to mild.
perceptions: My body or mind is not well.

variations.name: physical pain
variations.description: The body can be injured in many different ways, and pain is the way it tells us how urgently to seek relief.

guidance.description: Should I go to the doctor? Most of us have asked that question at one time or another. Whether it’s a bad cold, a funny-looking mole, or a nagging pain that just won’t go away,

variations.name: mental pain
variations.description: The mind can also be injured in many ways. It expresses a need for help with sensations ranging from minor anxiety to depression.

guidance.description: Sometimes it can be hard to tell when a concern about mental health signals a need for professional help. In certain situations, the answer is clear. But in others, it isn't so obvious. For example, if you're afraid of giving a speech in public, does it mean you have a mental health condition or just a typical case of nerves? Or, when does shyness become a social phobia? Here's help understanding how mental health conditions are identified.

variations.name: chronic pain
variations.description: Some kinds of pain do not heal so you have the knowledge that you will have to live with it.
perceptions: My body or mind is not well.
This has been going on a long time.

guidance.description: Living with chronic, persistent pain is a fact of life for 3 out of 10 people in the U.S. Chronic pain can develop in various ways, including from injury or illnesses. When pain lasts beyond three to six months, treatment focuses on the central nervous system, which includes the brain and spinal cord.

commentaries.quote: Pain is the body's way of saying 'be more careful please'.
Mysteriously and in ways that are totally remote from natural experience, the gray drizzle of horror induced by depression takes on the quality of physical pain.
Physical pain is far easier to bear than mental agony.
Living with chronic pain is like trying to get comfortable on a cactus sofa.
Pain is inevitable; suffering is optional.
